analysis: The 64-negative experiment executed successfully but did not improve validation: macro HR@10 was 0.5900 versus the stated 8-negative reference of 0.5925, a decrease of 0.0025. Electronics HR@10 fell from the stated 0.405 to 0.390. Current category HR@10 values were Movies_and_TV 0.640, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.610, Electronics 0.390, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.720. Macro HR@20 rose slightly from the stated 0.7075 to 0.7100, but this did not translate into better top-10 ranking. These results do not support the hypothesized benefit from increasing negative coverage; they do not establish a causal explanation or statistical significance. The host reported 51.79 allocated GPU-seconds. No test metrics were available.
code_summary: One independent LightGCN model per category, with 64-dimensional embeddings, three propagation layers, averaged initial and propagated embeddings, and a jointly learned item bias. The sole planned change increased the default uniform sampled-negative count from 8 to 64, yielding 65-class cross-entropy logits. Sampling rejects all observed training items and allows duplicate negatives. Training retains embedding regularization, Adam, seed 42, and validation-based selection of one checkpoint per category. The generated predictor routes all four datasets and scores candidates using the selected model’s propagated embedding dot products plus learned item bias; unseen users use the mean of their history item embeddings. No ensembles or separately fitted auxiliary scores are used.
